newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates surge to 29 pct as repo cut seen.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates surge to 29 pct as repo cut seen.

text.p: Hungary's overnight interbank interest rates soared to 29 percent on the last day of the two-week reserve period due to a shortage of funds caused by expectations for a repo cut, dealers said on Friday.
"There is a lot of money in government bonds and in reverse repo deals, even for one month, because of the expectations for the repo cut," Inter-Europa Bank's Balazs Varga said.

The overnight market, which closed at already high 23.50 percent levels on Thursday, opened at 26.00/28.50 on Friday, then quickly rose to 28.5/29.00 and remained at those levels for most of the session.
Banks hurried to fill their reserves on the last day of the period, when the market waited for a repo cut which has not come.
"Some players placed money at 23 percent with the central bank, expecting the cut, and now they took up money at 29 percent. It was not good business," a dealer said.
At the end of the session a player lent the remainder of excess funds at 23 percent but this did not change the picture of the session, characterized by unusually high rates.
